guides/CUES.html.summary: PlayForge — Cues A cue is what something shows and sounds, apart from what it changes: a spark as a hit lands, a hum while a shield holds, a shake as a giant falls. Effects, abilities, entities and items each list their cues, and a game's own code raises one where it likes. Every cue plays through ForgeCues, after Unreal's gameplay cues: a burst at a moment, as a hit's spark, or a lasting cue's beginning and its end, as a shield's hum, which share a key. Where cues are raised Effects: an effect's Cues component plays its cues as it lands, as an application it takes in lands, as each tick executes, as an impact it deals lands, as it comes off, while it lasts, as an application is refused and as its stacks change (EFFECTS.md). Abilities: a Cues component plays an ability's as it activates, as it commits, while it's active, as it ends and as one is refused; a Play Cue task plays them at a stage's exact moment, on the caster, on the target or at the point (ABILITIES.md). Entities: a Cues component plays an entity's as it spawns, dies and comes back, and lasting ones while it holds a tag, as stars over its head while it's Stunned (ENTITIES.md). Items: a Cues component plays an item's as it's equipped, while it's equipped and as it's used (ITEMS.md). Code: ForgeCues.Burst(sparks, new CueContext(entity, ECueMoment.Raised, point: hit.point)) plays sparks where a ray hit, and ForgeCues.Begin and ForgeCues.End begin and end a lasting one. A cue's context, CueContext, says what raised it, its Moment, as Applied, Activated or Died; its target and its source; the effect or the ability behind it; where it plays, its Point and Normal, or else its target's place; a magnitude; and, for a lasting cue, the key its beginning and its end share. Handlers Each cue in a list is a handler, its kind picked from the list. It plays at each moment whose list holds it, and, in a list of lasting cues, as a While Active, from its beginning to its end: Camera Shake shakes the camera through the shaker the game gives ForgeCues.Shaker, an ICameraShaker. Sound plays its clip where its Placement says (Placement). Prefab places its prefab where its Placement says, for its Lifetime, or, as a lasting cue, until its cue ends (Pooling). Floating Text floats a text where its Placement says, as a hit's damage, the gold a kill gave or a status's name (Floating text). Process runs a MonoBehaviour process where its Placement says, on a packet loaded for the cue, with its Data list last (Data packets): a burst's runs its own course, and a lasting one's runs until its cue ends (Pooling). Sequence runs a task sequence on a packet loaded for the cue, with its Data list last: a burst's runs its course, and a lasting one's runs until its cue ends. It goes by the clock its Clock picks, else the sequence's own, else that of the one it plays on. Cue Tag plays what its tag routes to (Routes). Write a handler of your own by deriving from AbstractCueHandler: override the moments it plays at, or Burst to play every burst one way, reading the moment from cue.Moment, and Begin and End for a lasting one. Placement A cue that places something, a Prefab or a Sound, says where with its Placement: At: on whom. Self: the one the cue is on: an effect's target, an ability's caster, the entity, or an item's holder. Where its raiser gave a point, as a hit's, it's there. Source: who's behind it, as an effect's source or a death's killer. Target: an ability's first target, or the place it targeted. For another's cue, the one it's on. Each Target: one at each of an ability's targets. Point: the cue's point, or the place an ability targeted. Socket: a child of theirs it's placed at, by name, found at any depth, as a hand or a weapon's tip. Offset moves it, and Scatter moves it by a random amount up to that much either way on each axis, both in the space of what it's placed at. Attach: whether it follows them: a lasting cue's only, by default; always; or never. An attached sound plays from a source of its own under them. Facing: as what it's placed at faces, or along the cue's normal at a point; along the cue's normal; away from or toward its source; or the world's way. Scatter draws from ForgeCues.Random, the cues' own random numbers, so a cue never moves the game's rolls: a server that plays no cues and a client that plays them must draw alike. Floating text A Floating Text cue floats a text where its Placement says, 2 units above the one the cue is on by default: a hit's damage, the gold a kill gave, a status's name as it lands. Text: what it says. {value} is its number, {name} the name of what raised it, as an effect's, and {tag} its cue tag: +{value} gold, or {name} for a status. Value: its number, From the cue's magnitude, as a hit's value from an effect's On Hit, or its Number, read as it plays, as a Tracked Impact's for the gold an instant effect gave. It's written with up to Decimals decimals; without its sign where Absolute says, as damage shown as 35; with a Plus Sign above 0; shortened past a thousand where Abbreviate says, as 1.2k; and not at all for 0 where Hide Zero says. Look: its Color, or its Negative Color below 0 where By Sign says; its Size, Font, Bold and Outline; turned to the camera where Face Camera says, ForgeCues.Camera or else the main camera; and its Sorting Order. A Prefab holding a TextMeshPro text shows it in place of the cue's own, its font, size and outline its own. Motion: its Lifetime; its Velocity, and a Random Velocity either way on each axis; Gravity, for an arc, and Drag; its opacity over its life, Fade, and its scale, Scale, as a pop; on the game's clock where Game Time says, else in real time. Stacking, on one entity: a number Merge Within some seconds of the last adds to it, which shows the sum and floats again, as a burn's ticks; each text floats a Stagger above the one below it, in the lowest place free; and at most Max Shown float at once, the oldest going first. Its texts come from ForgeCuePool and go back to it. For damage numbers, put one in an effect's On Hit: it plays as each impact the effect deals lands, on the one it lands on, told the value it changed. Routes A Cue Tag cue names a tag, as Cue.Hit.Fire, in place of what it shows, so an effect, an ability and an entity can each raise Cue.Hit.Fire and one place says how it looks. That place is the project's Cue Library, an asset from Create > PlayForge > Cue Library, which Project Settings > PlayForge names under Forge Project. Each of its routes is a cue tag and the handlers it plays. A tag plays its own route, or else its nearest parent's: with no route for Cue.Hit.Fire, Cue.Hit's plays. A route that doesn't Override plays its parent's after it, so Cue.Hit.Fire's flames add to Cue.Hit's spark. An entity's Cue Receiver component plays a tag its own way first, in place of the library's, or before it with Pass Through. Its Variant plays the library's route under its name, as Cue.Hit.Golem for Cue.Hit, where the library has one, so a golem's hit sounds of stone. Code can give a library of its own, ForgeCueRoutes.Library, in place of the project's. Raised The Cue Library's inspector lists under Raised each cue tag the project's assets raise through it, by a Cue Tag cue, in tag order. Each tag shows what plays it, "plays its own route", "plays Cue.Hit's route" or "plays nowhere", then a row for each asset that raises it, which opens the asset in The Forge. The section's header counts the tags, and how many of them play nowhere. It follows the project as it changes, and the library's routes as they're edited. The Problems view notes a Cue Tag cue that plays nowhere: one that names no tag; one whose project names no Cue Library; one whose tag the library routes nowhere, neither its own route nor a parent's. It's a note, not a warning, as an entity's Cue Receiver may play the tag its own way. An edit to the library, or to the library a project names, checks every asset again. Pooling A Prefab cue with Pooled takes its objects from ForgeCuePool and gives them back as its cue ends, a burst's after its Lifetime, in place of making and destroying one each time; the pool makes Preallocate of them ahead as the cue first plays. An IPooledCue on the prefab is told as it's taken and as it's given back, to reset it. A Process cue with Pooled does the same through CuePoolInstantiator, the instantiator its process's registration gives: each object comes from the pool, placed where the cue's packet says, and goes back as its process ends. Data packets A cue that runs a process or a sequence hands it a data packet of its own, loaded for what raised the cue, CuePackets.For(cue, data). It loads in four steps, each step's keys taking the place of an earlier step's: An ability's activation: an ability's cue starts from a copy of its activation's packet, with its targets, its targeting data and the numbers its caller set. The cue's context: the cue itself under Tags.CUE, a CueContext; its asset under Tags.ASSET, the effect, the ability, the item or the entity's identity, and its spec under Tags.SPEC, the effect's, the ability's or the item's; its source under Tags.SOURCE, and the one it plays on under Tags.TARGET_REAL where the activation named no target; where it plays under Tags.POSITION and Tags.ROTATION, and what it follows under Tags.TRANSFORM; its owner's clock: the activation's for an ability's cue, else that of the one it plays on. The asset's Local Data: each row under its key, its numbers read for the cue, as at its level. The cue's own Data list, last, so it has the last word. A row with no value puts nothing. A process or a sequence reads it as it reads any packet: data.TryGetFirst(Tags.CUE, out CueContext cue). Raises and sinks Each raise of a list of cues names what the list belongs to, its CueSource: an effect, an ability, an entity or an item, by its asset; a cue tag raised from code, as ForgeCueRoutes.Burst(cue); or a game's own code, where it names nothing. Code can name one: ForgeCues.Burst(cues, cue, CueSource.Of(effect)). Before any cue of a raise plays, its world's sink is asked, once: ForgeCueSink.WillPlay(event, raise), the raise holding the cue and its source. The default plays everything. A world of its own takes a sink of its own with ForgeCues.UseSink(world, sink), and ForgeCues.Sink is the one every other world asks. It's asked whatever mutes a cue, so a server that plays none can still send them on, as a network layer's sink does. A cue tag raised from code asks once; its routes, and a Cue Tag within them, play inside that raise, unasked. An effect's applier can say where it hit, before applying it: spec.WithHit(point, normal, magnitude). Its cues then play at the point, facing the normal, with the magnitude, as a sword's spark where the blade struck. Silencing and listening ForgeCues.Enabled = false silences every cue, as on a server or while a simulation runs ahead. ForgeCues.Mute(entity, true) silences one entity's, as one off screen. A lasting cue that began still ends. ForgeCues.Played hears each cue as it plays, for a debugger or a recorder.

guides/EFFECTS.html.title: PlayForge — Gameplay Effects | PlayForge
guides/EFFECTS.html.summary: PlayForge — Gameplay Effects A Gameplay Effect asset describes a change to an entity: damage, a heal, a timed buff, a poison, a cost or a cooldown. An entity is anything that runs a gameplay ability system (GAS), such as the player or an enemy. Abilities and items apply effects to a target entity, and so can your code. The ability, item or entity that applies an effect is its origin. An effect can change attributes (numbers such as Health), grant tags, apply other effects and run workers. The duration's Policy decides how long an effect lives. An Instant effect makes its change once and is done. A Durational or Infinite effect goes on the target's effect shelf, its list of active effects, and stays until its time runs out or something removes it. The kind of change follows from that: Effect Delivery The change Instant OnApply one permanent commit, such as "take 30 damage" Durational or Infinite, no ticks Continuous a modifier while the effect is active, reversed exactly when it ends Durational or Infinite, periodic ticks Periodic one permanent commit per tick, such as "5 Health per second" A commit stays after the effect ends. A modifier doesn't. EFFECT_PIPELINE.md has the full model. Tags are names, such as State.Stunned, that an entity carries and that requirements check. Each asset stores a tag made from its Name: Fireball Damage gives Effect.FireballDamage. Each section below matches the inspector section of the same name. Identity Name: the effect's display name. It also gives the asset tag, so renaming the effect changes its tag. Update anything that names the old tag. Description: free text for your UI. Asset Tag: read-only, made from the Name: punctuation is dropped, and each word is capitalised and joined. The tag is stored when you edit the Name. If the stored tag differs from the one the Name gives, it shows in warning text with an Update button that stores the new one. The effect system finds an effect by this tag when it is applied again or removed, whoever applied it. While a Durational or Infinite effect is active, its target carries the tag. Cooldowns work this way: an ability's Cooldown check looks for the cooldown effect's tag on the caster. Visibility: a tag your UI can read to decide whether to show the effect, such as Always Visible or Not Visible. The Forge lists it. The runtime doesn't act on it. Textures: icons, each paired with a tag. The texture tagged Primary is the effect's icon. Without one, the first texture is used. Inherit From Origin: its icon is its origin's, the ability, item or entity that applied it: the origin's texture under Origin Texture, a tag, Primary to start, which shows under it. Where the origin has none under that tag, the effect's own stands. A spec reads it, spec.GetIcon(), as the Demo's bar and the Additional Content's status bar do; an origin holds textures through IHasTextures, as abilities, items, effects, entities and both hubs do. Leveling An effect has no level of its own. At runtime it takes the level of its origin. Its scalers use that level to pick per-level values, such as 20/30/40/50 damage at levels 1 to 4. A scaler is a value source, such as a table with one value per level. A level provider is the asset whose level range an effect is authored for, normally its origin. Link Mode: Standalone (default): the effect takes the level of what applies it, as a note says. Linked To Provider takes the range from a level provider. Level Provider, while linked: the asset the range comes from, an Entity, Ability, Effect, Item or Attribute Set. Right-click the field to pick from one type. A link that would make a loop is refused, with an error in the Console. While no provider is set, a warning says the effect takes the level of what applies it. Starting Level and Max Level show the provider's range, read-only. Link Contained Effects, while linked, links every contained effect (see Impact) to this effect's provider, so their per-level values follow its range. Unlink Contained Effects removes the links that point at it. Each asks first, and one Undo takes it back. The link serves the inspector: a scaler set to Lock To Level Provider shows one value per level of the provider. An effect field in another inspector, such as an ability's Cost, says how the effect takes its levels, and its Link links the effect to that asset. Tags Granted Tags are applied to the target while the effect is active. An Instant effect grants them only for the moment it applies. Granted Abilities are given to the target as the effect lands, each at the level of what applied it, and taken back as it comes off. One that's running then is interrupted. An ability the target can't take, such as one it knows already when duplicates aren't allowed, isn't lent, so the target keeps its own as the effect comes off. An Instant effect lends none, as it's never on the target. A change of the target's sides while the effect lasts is a Side Change component (Side Change). Context Tags describe the effect, such as Fire. Each change the effect makes carries these and its origin's context tags, and workers can filter by them. They are not applied to the entity. Removes Effects Tagged makes the effect a cleanse. As it lands, every other effect on the target tagged with one of these, or a child of one, by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants, comes off, at the next tick, as a removed effect does. Status.Debuff takes off Status.Debuff.Poison and Status.Debuff.Burn, and State.Burning takes off whatever grants it. Purges makes the effect a purge, by the project's purge levels (Purging): as it lands, the effects on the target its strength reaches, of the kinds it names and applied by whom it says, come off. Blocks Effects Tagged makes the effect an immunity. While it's on the target and its ongoing requirements hold, an effect tagged with one of these, or a child of one, the same way, can't land, and applying it returns false. It leaves the effects already on the target; add the same tags to Removes Effects Tagged to clear them as it lands. Purging A project's Purge Levels, under Forge Project in Project Settings → PlayForge, rank its purges. Each Tier is a tag, weakest first, as Purge.Basic, Purge.Strong; an effect is at the first tier whose tag it carries, as its asset tag or a context tag, or a child of one. A purge of a tier takes the effects at that tier or under it, as a Strong dispel takes the Basic too, and an effect at no tier is never purged, but by death. A purge, an effect's Purges or ForgePurge.Purge(entity, purge) in code, has a Strength, a tier's tag; its Kinds, tags an effect must carry one of to be taken, as Status.Debuff, or any where it names none; Applied By, whom it takes the effects of, by who applied each against the one purged: itself, its allies (its buffs) or its enemies (its debuffs), an applier sharing none of its sides an enemy; and Filters of a project's own, each an AbstractPurgeFilter whose Takes says yes or no, as Except Tagged spares the effects carrying the tags it names. An effect a purge takes comes off at the next tick, as a removed effect does, and a purge never takes the effect doing it. ForgePurge.Purge(entity, strength) purges by a strength alone, of every kind. A staying entity's death purges its effects too, all but those it keeps: each tier's Kept On Death keeps the effects at it, and the table's Kept On Death categories keep theirs whatever their tiers, an ability's cooldowns, lent effects and toggles as a project starts (ENTITIES.md). Duration The fields show as the Policy uses them. Policy: Instant (default) makes the change once. Durational stays for a set time. Infinite stays until something removes it. Duration (Durational): the effect's length in seconds, with its scaler. Periodic Ticks (Durational and Infinite): a tick makes the effect's change again, as a new commit. Ticks (Durational): how many ticks fit in the duration, evenly spaced. The last falls as the duration ends, so 5 ticks over 10 seconds tick every 2 seconds. Tick Every (Infinite): the seconds between ticks. Tick On Application: run one tick as soon as the effect is applied, before the first periodic tick. It runs again when re-application refreshes or extends the effect. Use it with Periodic Ticks. On its own, it is a shape that the Problems view flags. Additional Executions (while it ticks): each tick executes the change a number of times, N plus this, combined with its scaler. N comes from the effect's container and is normally 1. A stacking container that shares one duration, or takes it from one stack, uses its stack count. Real Delta Time and Delta Time Scaler (Durational) change how fast the effect's clock runs. With no scaler, the clock follows Unity's frame time. With one, Real Delta Time combines the two. Multiply With Scaler, for example, slows the clock down or speeds it up. A tick only executes while the While On requirements hold (see Requirements). Re-application (Durational and Infinite) What happens when the effect is applied to a target that already has it. Each application on the shelf lives in a container. The effect is matched by its asset tag, whoever applied it. Re-application: Add Another (default) adds a separate container, and both apply. Do Nothing adds nothing new. Replace Existing gives the old container the new application's values and modifiers, and keeps its stack count. Past commits stay. Stack Existing adds stacks to the old container (see Stacking). Then (all but Add Another) applies as the old container takes in the application. Do Nothing (default) leaves its time alone. Refresh Duration restarts it. Extend Duration adds the new duration to it. Refresh and Extend also run Tick On Application again. Stacking (Stack Existing only) Stacking: Stacks Share One Duration (default) runs one timer for all stacks, and adding a stack doesn't reset it. Stacks Have Independent Durations gives each stack its own timer and ticks. Stacks drop off one at a time, and the effect lasts as long as its longest stack. Duration Taken From One Stack runs one stack's timer at a time. Each time it runs out, one stack is lost and the timer restarts. Stack Behaviours: optional stacking rules, such as Stack Bounds Config, which keeps the stack count between a Min and a Max, and Starting Stacks, the stacks a new effect starts with, each a number field read at the effect's level; Starting Stacks is one, where a number, a scaler, a combine and a rounding of its own were one written out. An application that would take the effect past the Max overflows: its Overflow Effects land, from the same origin, as a bleed's fourth stack hemorrhages, on the target or, with Overflow Lands On set to Caster, on its caster, as a frenzy; Deny Refresh On Overflow keeps that application from refreshing or extending the effect; and Clear Stacks On Overflow takes the effect's stacks off. Stack Amount, with its scaler: the stacks each application adds. 0 counts as 1. A change reads the stack count through an Effect Stacks scaler (SCALERS.md): a magnitude of −5 with Multiply With Scaler takes 5 a stack. A Continuous one updates whenever the count changes. A Periodic one lands once for each stack already, so one that reads its stacks counts them twice, 3 stacks hitting 9 times as hard as 1: the Problems view warns of it, and its quick fix, Count Stacks Once, gives the number one stack gives. Moving an effect to another entity gas.GetEffectSystem().MoveTo(effect, other) moves each of the effect's containers on the entity onto another, as a possession hands a body's effects over. Each keeps its stacks, its time left and what applied it. A move is neither a removal nor an application: none of either's workers, commits or contained effects run, and neither is told. Its lasting changes, its granted tags, the abilities it lends and its lasting cues go with it. Impact The impact is the change the effect makes to an attribute. The first fields are its first impact, whose delivery the duration gives it. Additional Impacts change more attributes, or the same one again, each with a delivery of its own. Attribute: the attribute to change. Leave it empty for an effect that only grants tags, applies other effects or runs workers. A target that lacks the attribute isn't changed. Operation: how the impact changes the attribute, and which of its two values, in one choice, such as Add to Current or Multiply Base. Base is the value the attribute is measured against, and Current is the value in play. For Health, Base is the maximum and Current is what is left. Add adds the magnitude. Use a negative magnitude to subtract. Multiply multiplies by it. Override sets the value to it. Flat Bonus adds too, but as a modifier it lands after the attribute's multipliers, so they don't scale it. Multiply Behaviour (Multiply only): Multiplicative (default) compounds with other multipliers, so ×1.5 and ×1.5 give ×2.25. Additive Bonus adds the bonuses first, so +50% and +50% give ×2.0. Add Behaviour (Add only, shown where it matters): as the attribute's role says, a Resistance's adds diminishing; a plain Sum; or Diminishing, on what's left (ATTRIBUTES.md). Pipeline: the calculation each hit of the impact goes through as it lands, a Value Pipeline: the caster's bonuses, the target's reductions, a critical roll, a barrier. It runs for an instant impact's hit and each tick of a periodic one (VALUE_PIPELINES.md). Magnitude: the amount: a Constant number, or by its kind a scaler's value at the origin's level, such as a By Level table of values per level, with Combine joining the scaler and the number (SCALERS.md). A Continuous modifier works its magnitude out again whenever the attribute is recalculated. A commit works it out once. A Set By Caller scaler reads a magnitude the code sets as it applies the effect, under a tag: on the spec with SetByCaller(tag, magnitude), or on an ability activation's data, which each effect the ability applies takes as it's made, its cost, cooldown and contained effects among them. Only the tag itself matches, and where none is set it reads its Default. A magnitude can also read what the effect has dealt, a part of another effect, ability or item on either side, or what a worker answers; SCALERS.md lists each kind. Delivery, read-only: when the impact lands, which the duration gives it (see the table above). On applying, While the effect lasts, or Each tick, which adds ", and on applying" when Tick On Application is on. A note says when Tick On Application alone keeps a multiply or override as a modifier, so it reverses as the effect ends. Commits, read-only, for a periodic impact: how many times it lands at the effect's first level, as in "7 over 6 s, level 1". For an Infinite effect, it says how far apart the ticks are. Impact Types: tags that label the kind of change, such as Damage.Fire. Workers can accept or skip changes by type. Never Allow hides the change from workers that check types. Always Allow passes every type check. Affiliation decides which targets the effect can be applied to. An entity's affiliation tags are its team or faction, set on its Entity asset. If the check fails, the effect isn't applied. Always Allow (default) allows any target. Affiliated allows targets that share the origin's affiliation, and Unaffiliated allows those that don't. Use Affiliation List compares the target with the Affiliations list instead. Comparison (all but Always Allow): Any (default) needs one tag to match. All needs every tag to match. The inspector no longer shows Reverse On Removal. A Continuous modifier always reverses when the effect ends, and a commit never does, so the flag changes nothing. The Problems view still flags a periodic effect that sets it. Additional Impacts Each additional impact changes an attribute of its own, or the same one again, with a delivery of its own. One effect can lower Armor while it lasts and burn Health on each tick. Add Impact adds one with a delivery the duration can make: Continuous on a Durational or Infinite effect, On Apply on an Instant one. While it's folded, an impact shows one line, such as "Mana −10 · Continuous", and its trash button removes it. Each has: Attribute, Operation, Multiply Behaviour and Magnitude, as above. Delivery: Continuous lasts while the effect does, then reverses. On Apply lands once, as the effect is applied. Periodic lands on each tick, and as the effect is applied when Tick On Application is on. It offers what the duration can make: an Instant effect makes only On Apply impacts, and Periodic needs ticks. If the duration changes so that an impact's delivery can't happen, a warning under it says so, and the impact never applies. Order (Override only): among overrides of one attribute, the lowest order wins. Retention Group: the group the change counts toward. Empty, it takes the effect's. Impact Types, as above. An impact with no Attribute changes nothing. The Cost check counts every attribute a cost spends (see ABILITIES.md). Contained Effects Other effects this one applies, with the same origin. Each row pairs a moment with an effect: On Apply (when this effect is applied), On Tick (on each execute tick) or On Remove (when this effect is removed); and says whom it lands on: the Target, this effect's, as it always did, or the Caster, as a lifesteal's heal or a curse's rebound as it ends. An Instant effect has no ticks and no removal, so only its On Apply rows run. An effect that is asked to apply again while it is still applying is refused, with a warning, so an effect that contains itself doesn't loop forever. Retention Group The group this effect's changes count toward (default Ignore), unless an impact names its own. Groups split an attribute's value for queries and UI, such as base and bonus health. They never change the math. Levels What the effect does, level by level. Its line, which the effect's header and The Forge's Summary column show, is its first impact by level, an add signed, as "-10/-20/-30 Health" or "+20 Armor", at its provider's levels where it's linked to one and at levels 1 to 5 where it isn't. ForgeAssetLines.Of(asset) gives any asset's line in the editor. The whole reading is code's, for a tooltip or a game's own screen: AbilityInspector.BuildEffectSeries(effect, 1, 5, caster, target) reads the effect at levels 1 to 5 against a caster and a target, either of which may be null. Each impact gives its Magnitude and Total at each level, its Line, as its field's summary reads it, its Parts at each level, and what it Needs; the effect gives its Duration, Ticks, Interval, Chance and Contained effects, and Describe(level) says what it does at a level, an impact to a line: "-15 Health each tick, 12 ticks over 12 s". NumberTrace.Of(number, context) explains any one number the same way, each part with what it read and what it gave: Health as it lands, level 2: -1 × (Caster's Attack Damage + 80 if Caster's Combo Charges > 0, else 0) = -100 Group = 100 Add: Caster's Attack Damage = 100 Add: Conditional = 0 When: Caster's Combo Charges > 0: doesn't hold False: 0 = 0 A read given no caster or no target gives, for a part that reads one, what its field falls back to, and says what it needs, as "the target". A kind or a condition of your own adds its parts by overriding Explain: trace.Add(Min, context, this, "Min"). Cues What the effect shows and sounds, apart from what it changes, plays from its Cues component, from the Components list's +, a list for each of its moments: On Apply as it lands; On Reapply as an application it takes in lands, as a stack or a refresh; On Tick as each tick executes; On Hit as an impact it deals lands, on the one it lands on, its magnitude the value it changed, as for a damage number; On Remove as a lasting effect comes off; While Active while it lasts, from as it lands, or a load puts it back, to as it comes off, ending as it began where another application replaced it; On Refused as an application is refused, as by an immunity, on the one it was aimed at; and On Stack Change as its stacks change while it lasts, its magnitude the stacks it has. An effect holds one at most. A cue plays at each moment whose list holds it: a sound on each tick is a Sound in On Tick, and one as the effect lands as well is in On Apply too. An applier can say where an application hit, spec.WithHit(point, normal, magnitude), and its cues play there (CUES.md). Each list's cues are listed as its workers are, each cue's kind picked from the list: Camera Shake: shakes the camera through the shaker the game gives ForgeCues.Shaker, an ICameraShaker. With none given, it shakes nothing. Its Strength and Duration, as Prefab's Lifetime and Sound's Volume, are number fields read for its effect as it plays. Sound: plays its clip where its Placement says, at the target by default (CUES.md). Prefab: places its prefab where its Placement says, at the target by default, for Lifetime seconds, or, in While Active, for as long as the effect lasts, following the target. A cue raised at a point, as a Play Cue task's, places it there. With Pooled it takes its objects from a pool and gives them back, ForgeCuePool, the pool making Preallocate of them ahead as it first plays, and an IPooledCue on the prefab resets it as it's taken and given back. Floating Text: floats a text where its Placement says, as a hit's damage or a status's name (CUES.md). Process: runs a MonoBehaviour process where its Placement says, on a data packet loaded for the cue, as a shield's while it lasts (CUES.md). Sequence: runs a task sequence on a data packet loaded for the cue, as a flicker while the effect lasts (CUES.md). Cue Tag: plays what its tag routes to (CUES.md). A save's load ends each While Active cue and begins it again as the effect leaves and comes back, and plays no burst. Write a cue of your own by deriving from AbstractCueHandler and overriding the moments it plays at, or Burst to play every burst one way, reading the moment that raised it from cue.Moment. Every cue plays through ForgeCues, an effect's as any other's. A game's own code raises one there too, as sparks where a ray hit: ForgeCues.Burst(sparks, new CueContext(entity, ECueMoment.Raised, point: hit.point)). A cue's context says what raised it, who's behind it, where it plays and, for a lasting cue, the key its beginning and its end share. ForgeCues.Enabled = false silences every cue, as on a server or while a simulation runs ahead, and ForgeCues.Mute(entity, true) one entity's, as one off screen; a lasting cue that began still ends. ForgeCues.Played hears each cue as it plays, for a debugger or a recorder. A Cue Tag cue plays what its tag routes to, in place of naming what it shows, so an effect, an ability and an entity can each raise Cue.Hit.Fire and one place says how it looks. The project's Cue Library, an asset its settings name, plays the route for the tag, or else for its nearest parent, and a route that doesn't Override plays its parent's after it. An entity's Cue Receiver component plays a tag its own way first, in place of the library's, or before it with Pass Through; its Variant plays the library's route under its name, as Cue.Hit.Golem for Cue.Hit, where the library has one. CUES.md brings cues together: where each is raised, the library's routes, what each tag plays, and pooling. Requirements Chance to Apply comes first: how likely the effect is to land, from 0 to 1, which can scale by level. It gates the whole application, as the Applying rows do. Each application draws once from PlayForge's random source (ForgeRandom), and a miss is refused, so applying returns false, as an immunity's refusal does, and the target's callbacks hear it, OnEffectRefused, with why (ENTITIES.md). 1, the default, always lands, and 0 never does; neither draws, so an effect without a chance leaves the numbers others draw as they were. A contained effect draws its own: a strike with a bleed at 0.3 lands every time, and its bleed about one time in three. The section's summary shows a chance short of 1. Chance Roll, under it, says how the chance rolls, as every chance PlayForge rolls can, and shows for a chance that can miss: Pseudo Random: each miss raises the next roll's odds by a constant and a hit starts them again, so streaks even out and the chance over many rolls stays the same, as Dota's pseudo-random distribution: a 25% chance's first roll has about 8.5%, its next about 17%, and so on. Each caster keeps its own streak for each chance. Luck: the attribute playing the project's Luck role (ATTRIBUTES.md), read on the caster, or with Own Luck a number of the chance's own, its Luck, shown under Own Luck alone: above 0 it rolls that many more times and keeps the best, below 0 the worst. A chance of 1 or more always comes up and one of 0 or less never does, and neither draws. The same roll is on a trigger's Chance, the Chance stage of a Value Pipeline, an ability's Chance to Activate, and the Chance condition, which holds on a roll of its number, as a critical strike chance read from an attribute: in a hit it rolls once and keeps the roll, so a hit read twice, its preview and its commit, reads the same. Under it are tag checks against the effect's target, and against its source, the entity behind its origin. The switch shows one side's table at a time: On the target first, then On the source. Each table has a row for each group: Applying: must pass for the effect to be applied. The effect is also refused if its Removed By row is already met. While on: while it fails, the effect stays, but its ticks don't execute. Its Continuous modifiers stay in place. Removed by: when it's met, the effect is removed. Each row has two cells. Requires lists the tags the entity must have, and Must not have the tags it must not have, or says None. A row passes when the entity has every tag it requires and none it must not have. Click a cell to edit its list under the table, with the row's Template, a shared Requirement Template, and Sync With Template, which keeps the row's tags the same as its template's. A template's Category is a tag of its own context, Requirement Category, which groups templates. Each entry is a tag query: a Tag, a Match mode and a comparison with a number, where Greater Than 0 means "the tag is present". Empty Applying and While On rows always pass. An empty Removed By row never removes anything. While On and Removed By are checked whenever an effect is applied to or removed from the target. While On is also checked before each tick. Under the tables are its Conditions for each phase, each a condition read in the effect's context, its caster's and its target's numbers in reach, as "the target below 30% Health". Apply Conditions must each hold for it to land; Ongoing Conditions pause it while one fails, as While On does; and Removal Conditions take it off once each holds, with its Removed By rows where it names any, as Attribute Shift stops at its floor. A phase passes only when its tags pass and its conditions all hold. The Ongoing and Removal conditions are checked at the entity's end of frame while the effect lasts, as no tag needs to change for an attribute they read to, and before each tick as well. Components An effect's components are features it carries, each a class with hooks into its life, added with the list's +. A component hears the effect Land on the entity it's on, Tick each period, Hit as an impact it deals lands, and End as it comes off: an instant effect at once, a lasting one as it's removed, at the moments its workers do; and Death as the one it's on dies while it's on them, whether the entity stays or ends, before what the death ends comes off. A lasting effect's components hear it Lend what it gives while it lasts, as it starts to last: as it lands, before its Land, as it takes another's place under its tag, and as a load or a move puts it back, where it doesn't land again; and TakeBack, as it stops: as it comes off, before its End, as another takes its place, and as a load clears it or a move takes it away. An Aura lends its aura so. A kind that makes no sense twice is offered only while the effect holds none of it. It hears Reapply as an application it takes in lands, as a stack or a refresh; Refused as an application of it is refused, with why, on the one it was aimed at; and StacksChanged as its stacks change while it lasts, with the counts before and after. It hears a tick only as one executes: one its ongoing condition stops isn't heard. A component of your own derives from AbstractEffectComponent and overrides the hooks it needs, each a no-op otherwise. It's the effect's, shared by everything that holds it, so what it keeps for one application of it it keeps through its context: ctx.GetState<T>(this). Describe says what it does in one line with its numbers, as an Area's "Lands on enemies within 300", which the Components section's line and The Forge's summary say beside its name. Auras An Aura component holds an effect on those near the one it's on, while it lasts. Items, abilities and entities have one too, each its own kind. Each has the Effect it holds, a Radius from its holder, read at each check, Flat, whom it Takes by how each stands to its holder, its Allies, itself among them, to start, and an Interval, 0.25 s by default, at which it checks who's near, by its holder's own time. It puts its effect on each that comes near, from an origin of its own, and takes it off as they leave, die or end, as its holder dies or ends, or as the aura goes; an effect of its that ends on its own, a durational one, goes on again at its next check. An Infinite effect holds as long as they're near. Two of an item hold two, as their effect's stacking says. A purge counts an aura's effect Lent. Each Aura component gives its aura in its own hooks: an effect's as it lends, an ability's as it's granted, an item's as it's equipped, an entity's as it registers. An entity's auras are its AuraSet, gas.GetService<AuraSet>(), a service it steps (ENTITIES.md), and ForgeAuras.Provide(entry, holder) and Remove give one of your own. Area An Area component lands the effect on those near its target as it lands, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits: each within its Radius of the target, read as it lands, along the ground unless Flat is off; of those it Takes by how each stands to its caster: its Enemies, its Allies, itself among them, its Other Allies, Self, All But Self or Everyone (a caster with no sides takes everyone as its allies and enemies); and at most Max Targets besides the target, the nearest first, or every one at 0. Each is found by its position, with no collider. Each takes the effect from the same origin, so its modifiers and its chance to apply are its own, and an effect that lands by an area spreads no further. A Radius of 0 is no area. It lands on its target and those it takes in the project's resolve order, its target among them, unless its Use Resolve Order is off (see Resolve Order). An effect holds one at most; without one, it lands on its target alone. Transfers A Transfer component moves an amount from one attribute to another, as Essence Shift steals Agility or Attribute Shift moves Agility into Strength. From, the effect's caster or its target, gives its From Attribute, and To gets its To Attribute, each side its own, so an entity can give to itself. Slot says which values move: Current, as a pool's Mana; Base; or Current And Base, as a stat's Strength. Amount can scale by level. Only what the giver has moves, so one with 3 of a steal of 5 gives 3, and nothing is made. Delivery says when: On Apply moves once as the effect lands and Periodic each tick, both for good; Continuous moves as the effect lands and holds while it lasts, a modifier on each side, read again only where a stack or a level changes its amount, and gives back as the effect ends, as a load or a move takes it, or as the entity it's on goes. Each side's change is exact: no worker takes it for a hit, no barrier soaks it and nothing scales it, so the getter gets what the giver gave, as far as its own bounds let it; what its maximum can't hold is lost, as an overheal is. The Problems view warns of a transfer whose Delivery the effect's duration can't make, as it does an additional impact's, and of one that names no attribute to give or get, each numbered among the effect's transfers. An effect holds as many as it moves, each its own. Side Change A Side Change component changes the target's sides while the effect lasts: to its caster's, as they are as it lands (Source Caster, a mind control), or to the Sides it names (Named, a pacify's Neutral), which show under Named alone. Of several on one entity, the highest Priority holds, read as it lands, a tie going to the latest, and as the last ends its own sides come back. Its tags follow, so whom effects and areas take changes with it. Interrupts breaks what the target runs as the change lands or ends, where it changes the sides, not where a change of higher priority keeps them. An Instant effect doesn't last, so it changes nothing. An effect holds one at most; it was a field of the effect's own, Side Change in its Tags section, with a switch. Spread A Spread component spreads its effect, or the Effect it names, from the one it's on to those near them, at the moments its When names, any of them: as the effect Lands, each Tick, as it comes off (End), however it ends, or as the one it's on dies (Death), as a plague jumps from its victim to the enemies near it. It takes each within its Radius of the one it's on, read at the effect's level, along the ground unless Flat is off; of those it Takes by how each stands to its caster, its Enemies to start, as an Area's; at most Max Targets each time, the nearest first, or every one at 0; and passes over those who have the effect it spreads already, unless Skip Holders is off. Each takes the effect from the same origin, its caster's, so its modifiers and its chance to land are its own, in the project's resolve order unless Use Resolve Order is off. A landing it made spreads on only so far as its Hops allow: at 0, it spreads only from where the effect landed of its own; at 1, once more from each it spread to; and on. An effect holds as many as it has moments to spread at, each its own. Workers Effect workers react to this effect's own events. A worker can act when the effect is applied, when it ticks, when it is removed, and when it deals a change to an attribute (WORKERS.md maps each, and on whose side it runs). Workers return actions, which run at the end of the frame. An Instant effect runs its apply and remove workers within its one application. A worker can also answer numbers: a magnitude of the Worker kind asks the effect's workers for a value under a key, and one that implements INumberWorker answers, as the Attribute Change worker answers how much health the target has lost since the effect began. What a worker keeps for one application of its effect goes in ctx.GetState<T>(this), since the worker itself is shared by every application (SCALERS.md). Worker Group, after them, gives the one the effect is on more workers while it lasts, as an item's group does while it's equipped: attribute workers, as a debuff that changes how its target takes damage; impact, tag and analysis workers, as Ice Blast's debuff shattering its target as its Health falls below 13% by a Threshold. They come back as it goes. Two of the effect on one target give the group once, and the last of them to go takes it back. An Instant effect doesn't last, so its group does nothing. On Hit On Hit, above the workers, holds the effects the hits of the one this effect is on apply while it lasts: a poisoned blade, a boon's Weak. Its entries are an item's: an attribute, the effects, to the one hit or the holder, only on a kill, impact types and a condition (ITEMS.md). An Instant effect doesn't last, so its On Hit does nothing. Another effect that replaces it under its tag takes it off, and a load puts it back once. Proc Coefficient, in Impact, is what the effect's own hits carry for On Hit effects: theirs scale their chance and their duration by it, so a damage over time at 0.25 sets them off a quarter as often, for a quarter as long, and 0 sets nothing off. With Own Proc Coefficient off, its ability's stands, or else 1, and Proc Coefficient is hidden. An effect has no lifesteal of its own: what its hits heal its caster is the caster's Lifesteal, the attribute the Lifesteal worker names as its Share, which the worker heals by, the one the project gives every entity or the caster's own (WORKERS.md). For hits that steal more, an effect raises its caster's Lifesteal while they should: a lasting effect of +0.3 Lifesteal whose Removal condition takes it off, as a charged attack's buff comes off as its last charge is spent. The heal is a gain like any other, so Healing Received scales it, and damage a return sends back heals nothing. Resolve Order The project's Resolve Order, under Forge Project in Project Settings → PlayForge, decides the order an area's effects land on those it takes, so specific behaviour can be coded, as a totem whose aura keeps its allies alive resolving after them. Each entry is a Tag and an Order: one carrying the tag, or one under it, resolves at its Order, lower first, and one carrying none of the entries' tags at 0. One carrying several takes the first entry it matches, so the list's order is its precedence. An entity carries a tag on its identity, as a totem always does, or while something grants it, as an aura can grant its holder one while it holds. The area's own order breaks ties. Apply Effects and Apply/Remove Effects land on an ability's targets in it, though the targeting keeps its own order and its primary target; an effect's Area component lands on its target and those it takes in it, its target among them; and an aura puts its effect on those that came near in it. The tasks' and the Area's Use Resolve Order, on by default, turns it off for that one. Code reads it through ForgeResolveOrder: OrderOf(target), Sort(targets), and TargetsOf(data) for an activation's targets in order. A death waits for its entity's end of frame, and an aura comes off a dead holder at its next check or as the holder ends, so one area's hits resolve together: a blow that kills the totem doesn't take its aura off the hero the same explosion strikes next. The order matters for what changes as each lands, as an effect that lands on the caster with each hit or a transfer. Modifiers Modifiers, under On Hit, change other effects as they're made, for that application alone: a boon that adds a burst to every Chill its holder applies, a ring that makes its holder's debuffs last longer, a cloak that halves the stuns landing on its wearer. An effect's hold on the one it's on while it lasts; an item's, an ability's and an entity's modifiers are the same entries. Each entry is a rule of its own, or names a shared Effect Modifier asset (Create → PlayForge → Effect Modifier), whose rule it uses in its place. A rule has: Direction: Outgoing, its holder's own effects as it applies them, on another or itself; Incoming, the effects landing on its holder, whoever applies them; or Both. Effect Tags: the effects it changes, each with one of these among its asset tag and context tags, or a child of one, so Status.Chill picks every Chill. None picks every effect. When: a condition read as the effect is made, its caster the caster and its target the target. Changes, each of a kind: Add Contained Effect: an effect that lands as this one lands, each tick, or as it ends, on the target or, with Lands On set to Caster, on its caster. Change Impact: a Value Pipeline stage its impacts on an attribute go through, of some impact types where it names any. An impact that commits, a hit or a tick, runs it after its own pipeline, and its breakdown keeps it; a lasting impact, which no pipeline runs on, takes it on its magnitude, as Weak's −30% made −40%. Add Overflow Effect: an effect that lands as an application would take it past its most stacks, on the target or its caster as its Lands On says, and Clear Stacks, which takes its stacks off with it. It needs a stack bound of the effect's own to overflow. Change Duration: its time multiplied, then more added; its ticks spread over the time it has. Change Stacks: more it can hold at most, where a stack bound of its own sets a most, and more a landing gives. Change Chance to Apply: multiplied, then added to. Grant Tags: more tags it grants while it's on. An effect a rule adds, and what that effect contains, isn't changed by that rule again, so a Chill that adds a Chill adds one. Two of an item modify twice. Local Data Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Each row has a Key (a tag) and a value of a kind: Float, Int, String, Bool, Tag, Attribute, Effect, Ability, Entity, Object, MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject, or a kind of your own, a [Serializable] class made from LocalDataValue<T>, as a point or a colour, which the row's kinds offer beside PlayForge's. A row saves its own value alone. Object fields take project assets, not scene objects. Code reads a value by its type, data.TryGet(out float range) or data.TryGet(out MyPoint point), and a number, a Float or an Int, which can scale, with data.Value.TryReadNumber(context, out float number). PlayForge doesn't read an effect's Local Data itself. Your code and workers can, with effect.TryGetLocalData(key, out var data). The first row with that key wins. Used By The PlayForge assets that refer to this effect, each with its type icon, such as an ability whose cost it is or an item that grants it. Click a row to select the asset. The list follows the project as it changes.

guides/EFFECT_PIPELINE.html.summary: PlayForge — Gameplay Effect & Attribute Pipeline How a GameplayEffect becomes an attribute change, stays correct while it lives, and reverses when it dies — under the two-kind impact model. This is the authoritative description of the runtime pipeline; if code and doc disagree, one of them has a bug — file it either way. All paths relative to Assets/PlayForge/Runtime/PlayForge/. 1. The model in one page Every authored impact is an AttributeImpactEntry on GameplayEffectImpact.Entries: { AttributeTarget, Delivery, Operation, TargetSlot, MultiplyBehaviour, SortOrder, Magnitude, RetentionGroupOverride, ImpactTypes }. One effect may carry many entries across many attributes ("+10% speed while active AND 5 HP per tick" is one asset): the first derived from its impact's fields, then each of its AdditionalImpacts (§7). Delivery decides everything — there is deliberately no separate "retained?" or "reverse on removal?" switch: Delivery Kind When Reversal Continuous Modifier — transient, derived registered on apply, while the carrier lives automatic & exact: unregister + recompute. The ONLY reversal mechanism. OnApply Commit — permanent once at application never Periodic Commit — permanent once per execute tick never Modifier = "while this carrier is present" — item stat bonuses, auras, durational %-buffs. Its magnitude is re-evaluated on every recompute; removing the carrier recomputes without it. A ×1.2 buff can never leave residue because its value is never stored, always derived. Commit = an event that permanently changed the attribute — damage, heals, DoT/HoT ticks. The post-constraint delta is recorded into per-group committed history and survives everything. Retention groups (Tag) are pure attribution: every contribution — root value, modifiers, commits — belongs to a group (entry override → else the effect's Definition.RetentionGroup; attribute-set roots use their element's RetentionGroup). Groups partition one pool for queries/UI (base vs bonus health, base vs bonus damage); they never change the math. Validation: Continuous requires a durational/infinite effect; Periodic requires ticks. (AttributeImpactEntry.IsDeliveryValidFor.) 2. Attribute state (CachedAttributeValue) ActiveValue = ConstrainValue( ← element clamp + rounding ModifierPipeline( ← Add → Multiply → FlatBonus → Override root ← Blueprint.GetActiveValue(cache), re-derived + Σ committedByGroup ) ) ← fresh every recompute (or generic seed) State: modifiers — ordered (carrier, impacter, group) entries. Presence == contribution; no alive-flags, no zombie state. Re-registering a carrier replaces its entries (idempotent refresh — the stacking path relies on this). Removed entries are kept spare and reused, so a refresh allocates nothing. committedByGroup — permanent history per retention group. Written only by CommitImpact. Attribution — rebuilt on every Recompute; per-group slices that sum exactly to ActiveValue. 2.1 Recompute pipeline Baseline = the root value. Add — additive modifier impacters, per slot (Current / Base / CurrentAndBase) → DirtyValue. The sums first; then each add that diminishes, on what's left, 1 − (1 − x)(1 − v): every add on a Resistance attribute, unless its Add Behaviour says Sum, and any whose Add Behaviour says Diminishing. Multiply — Multiplicative impacters compound (×1.5, ×1.5 → ×2.25); AdditiveBonus impacters pool (eval − 1) into one ×(1 + Σ) (+50%, +50% → ×2.0). FlatBonus — post-multiplication additive. Committed history — all of it, where it was measured: after the modifiers, so a transient % modifier doesn't scale it. 50 base × 1.5 aura + 10 tome = 85, and a 30 hit under the aura takes 30. Override — per-slot, lowest SortOrder wins. It comes after the committed history, so an override ("stun: speed = 0") still pins the value. Constrain: element overflow clamp (AttributeOverflowData.Clamp) + rounding policy. Attribution is captured during the walk (root → its group; commits → their groups; each modifier → the value swing its op produced; pooled multiplies → proportional shares; the constraint shift → the unattributed slice) so GetBreakdown() always sums to ActiveValue. 2.2 Commit math CommitImpact(carrier, impacters) runs each impacter as a sequential mini-step against the live value (op → clamp → round), records each step's post-constraint delta into its group (a +50 heal clamped to +30 commits +30), then runs one canonical Recompute. Reproducibility invariant: ActiveValue is always exactly Recompute(state) — every mutation path ends in a recompute. There is no second bookkeeping system to drift. 2.3 Query surface GetGroupValue(Tag) / GetBreakdown() on CachedAttributeValue; TryGetGroupValue(attr, group, out v) / GetBreakdown(attr) on AttributeSystemComponent. Consumer pattern: UI splits a health bar by group slices; a damage formula reads GetGroupValue(damage, Group.Base) vs GetGroupValue(damage, Group.Bonus) and applies different outgoing calculations — group-specific math lives in consumers, not the pipeline. 3. The four-verb attribute API (AttributeSystemComponent) Every attribute mutation funnels through one shared 4-phase pipeline (CommitWithCarrier): pre-change workers → PHASE-2 dispatch → post-change workers → impact relay (ImpactData, frame summaries, source-side TrackImpact, AttributeChanged). Verb Dispatch Used by RegisterModifier(attr, smv, impacters) register/refresh in modifiers + recompute Continuous entries on apply / stack refresh / replace UnregisterModifier(attr, smv) remove carrier's entries + recompute removal & replacement — fires callbacks like any change, so regulated attributes refresh (removal used to be silent → stale derived values). It's no hit, though: its ImpactData.Ends holds, so its effect's workers and components hear no impact, its dealer's impact workers don't run and no Impact Taken or Dealt is sent CommitImpact(attr, smv, impacters) permanent per-group commit OnApply / Periodic entries ModifyAttribute(attr, smv) CommitImpact; a delta-only carrier's delta commits as constant Adds in its retention group init pulse, EnforceScaling propagation, external systems (TryModifyAttribute) Registration/unregistration are identity-based on the carrier instance — they are never wrapped in synthetic carriers. Pre-change phase (commits). Before the pre-change callback and workers run, a commit evaluates its impacters once (frozen as constants, so a randomized scaler can't roll differently twice) and previews the incoming delta: ops in order, no bounds or rounding. That delta is what ChangeValue holds, since effect specs arrive as (0,0) transport, and an Inline worker's edit is what commits: untouched → the frozen impacters commit as authored (op semantics, per-impacter groups); adjusted → the new delta commits as one constant Add in the impacters' shared group (mixed groups fall back to the carrier's retention group). Either way §2.2 applies: post-constraint delta recorded, then Recompute. Armor therefore acts on incoming damage and the clamp comes after: 20 HP, −30 hit, 50% armor → −15 → 5 HP. Raw deltas (ModifyAttribute) preview as themselves. Register/Unregister are observe-only here, because modifiers are re-derived every recompute, so a one-off adjustment has nowhere to live. A commit allocates nothing, adjusted or not. It rents its ChangeValue and its frozen impacters and gives them back when it's done, one set for each commit in progress, since a worker or a listener can commit inside another. An adjusted delta's Adds are frozen in the same impacters. So: a ChangeValue belongs to its commit. A callback or an Inline worker reads it during the call, or copies its Value, and doesn't keep it; a Deferred worker's actions may keep it. A change handed to one is left to them, and its commit takes a new one for the next; the source-side TrackImpact keeps a total, the last impact and a count, not every impact. A raw delta allocates nothing on its way through either: its delta's Adds are frozen in the same impacters, and a SourceAttributeImpact keeps the origin it makes. GenerateSimple makes a new carrier on every call, so a raw delta made every frame keeps its carrier, made once with IAttributeImpactCarrier.GenerateSourceDerivation(source, attribute). The changes the system makes on someone's behalf, EnforceScaling's rescale and the lifesteal worker's heal, allocate nothing either: each is carried by a carrier kept for its source and attribute, in a table keyed weakly by source, so a source that's gone isn't held; each deferred one is queued in a ModifyAttributeAction the system takes back once the queue has run it, so a listener of OnActionQueued or OnActionExecuted reads an action during the call. One the queue invalidates isn't taken back; the queue walks its priority buckets by index, and EnqueueRange reads a list or an array by index, so taking an action off allocates nothing. Null / undefined attribute targets early-out safely (pure tag-grant effects are legal). 4. Effect lifecycle (EffectSystemComponent) One shared component owns the shelf. Both RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem and the MonoBehaviour GameplayAbilitySystem forward to a GASCore, which holds it (public API unchanged). Edit EffectSystemComponent for effect logic and GASCore for the rest of the GAS, not the hub classes. ApplyGameplayEffect(spec) │ validate (affiliation + source/target tag requirements) ├─ Instant → grant tags → app workers → CommitImpact per OnApply entry │ → removal workers (every impact made; none when nothing committed) → remove tags └─ Durational/Infinite → TryHandleExistingDurationalGameplayEffect (absorbed? → done) → GenerateContainer → shelf (container ctor sets spec.RuntimeContainer + duration math); its tags count from here → RegisterModifier per Continuous entry → app workers → if TickOnApplication: tick workers once + CommitImpact per Periodic entry × executeTicks then: requirements left for the next tick → RecordEffectApplied + EffectApplied callback → contained OnApply effects (recursive; see §4.2 for the cycle guard) Tick (per update): if anything was applied since the last: HandleGameplayEffects (compile tags once → a met removal requirement finishes its container, ongoing requirements set Ongoing) EnablePeriodicTicks: timers advance → executeTicks → tick workers (every frame, even 0) → per execute tick: CommitImpact per Periodic entry + contained OnTick effects Remove (ClearFinishedEffects): the pass's finished containers off the shelf and the index together → each: OnRemove: ReverseImpact() = UnregisterModifier per Continuous entry, then contained OnRemove effects → removal workers → RecordEffectRemoved + EffectRemoved callback SourcedModifiedAttributeValue(spec, 0, 0) is transport only — magnitudes are always evaluated freshly by the impacter pipeline. 4.1 Re-application (ReApplicationPolicy) Policy Behavior DoNothing absorbed; only the interaction runs ReplaceOldContainer ReverseImpact() old spec → container adopts new spec (+durations; stack count preserved) → register new spec's Continuous entries. Old commits stay — commits never reverse. AppendNewContainer fresh container + distinct spec instance → modifiers coexist (stacking by coexistence; MultiplyBehaviour controls composition) StackExistingContainers Stack(n) on the found container → re-register Continuous entries so stack-aware magnitudes recompute now (ScalerImpacter evaluates container-aware via spec.RuntimeContainer). A stack lost when its time runs out re-registers the same way, as does the stack Extend adds to independent durations ReApplicationInteraction (Refresh/Extend + re-fire TickOnApplication) runs only when absorbed — the append path would double-tick otherwise. 4.2 Loop-safety invariants (do not undo) All finish paths go through MarkFinished (exactly-once; duplicate OnRemove = double reversal). A set mirrors the finished list, so marking a container and skipping a finished one never walk it. TickEffectShelf iterates by index over the frame-start count (contained effects add to the shelf mid-loop); already-finished containers are skipped. ClearFinishedEffects snapshots-and-clears, then takes the whole pass off the shelf and out of the index, in one walk of each, before any OnRemove. Taken off one at a time, each a linear remove, ending n containers cost n². A spec builds its impacters once, with each delivery's attributes and each attribute's impacters. GetImpactersFor returns the spec's own list: read it, don't change it. A tick's lookups, its contained effects and a recompute allocate nothing; walk the lists by index or with a foreach over the concrete type, since one through an interface boxes. Scaler-driven execute-tick counts are evaluated once per batch, never per loop iteration. An effect asked for again on an entity before its own application there is over is refused, with one warning per entity and effect. An effect that contains itself, directly or through other contained effects or what applying it sets off, recursed until the stack overflowed. Any change to a container's stack count re-registers its Continuous entries, gained or lost. Applying never walks the shelf. Its requirements wait for one pass at the next tick, a container's tags count from the moment it is shelved, and re-application finds its containers in an index by asset tag, which Shelve and Unshelve keep. Each application re-checked every container and rebuilt all tags, so it cost as much as the entity carried. 5. Recalculation (regulated attributes) Blueprint cached scalers register contact → dependent edges at attribute registration (ProvideAttribute → RegulateContactWith). Any commit or modifier registration or unregistration fires AttributeChanged → RefreshRegulatedAttributes(contact) → dependents Recompute (re-deriving their root from the contact's fresh ActiveValue while their own modifiers and committed history are preserved) → chained AttributeChanged, cycle-guarded. A dependent's refresh is the system's own change. It takes the post-change half of the pipeline: EnforceScaling, post-change workers and AttributePostChange. It is recorded in the frame summary as received and dealt, self to self. Its carrier is the attribute's root, typed DisallowImpact, so a worker that checks impact types passes it by. Effect-magnitude scalers that read attributes capture snapshots at apply time by design — only blueprint scalers create live dependencies. 6. Initialization & auto-scaling ProvideAttributeSet: register attributes → initialize each cached value (first recompute) → zero-delta ModifyAttribute pulse per attribute (callbacks observe initial values; no worker does, as the pulse runs none and is unworkable; commits nothing). EnforceScaling (AutoScaleWithBase): Base changes, a dependent's refresh included, enqueue a deferred proportional Current adjustment through a synthetic carrier, kept for whoever changed Base — lands as ordinary committed history. The carrier is typed DisallowImpact and unworkable, as the pulse is, so no worker that checks impact types sees it. The adjustment is a share of Current before the bounds, where it lands, so the bounds clamp the result once: under ZeroToBase an 80/100 attribute that loses half its Base ends at 40/50. 7. Entry derivation (no asset migration) The first entry is derived, never serialized. The effect's impact quad + duration flags are its authored surface; GameplayEffectImpact.RebuildEntries re-derives that entry on every Generate(), so inspector edits (magnitude, attribute target, duration policy, tick flags) always take effect on the next application. Magnitude on the derived entry references the live ScalableFloat, so even already-registered modifiers re-evaluate new magnitudes on their next recompute. Serializing the derived entry was tried and reverted: OnValidate froze half-authored state into assets (null targets, stale magnitudes, deliveries minted while the policy was still Instant) and never re-synced. Additional impacts are authored entries. GameplayEffectImpact.AdditionalImpacts holds AttributeImpactEntry values that the impact drawer edits, each naming its own delivery, and RebuildEntries appends them, live, after the derived entry. One with no attribute is skipped, and so is one whose delivery the duration can't make (IsDeliveryValidFor), which the drawer flags in place. Delivery derivation (ResolveDelivery): Authored shape Derived delivery Instant OnApply Durational/Infinite, no ticks Continuous + periodic ticks Periodic (ReverseImpactOnRemoval flagged: rollback no longer exists) TickOnApplication-only trap Continuous for Multiply/Override (flagged), else OnApply Window → PlayForge → Problems lists each effect that has one of the shapes above, among the validator's other problems — read-only, nothing is written. Deleted outright: IsSustainedModifier(), the Mode A/B inference, TickAttribute, RollbackCommittedDelta, tick-rollback via TrackedImpact (which is analytics-only now). 8. Verification Assets/PlayForge/Tests/Editor/PlayForgeGoldenTests.cs — the Test Runner's EditMode tab, FarEmerald.PlayForge.Tests.Golden (or batchmode -executeMethod FarEmerald.PlayForge.Tests.PlayForgeGoldenTests.RunAll). Scenarios pin: multiplicative/pooled buff add/remove ordering (the 50→60→72→60→50 case), item modifier reversal, HoT permanence through expiry, clamp + history reproducibility, committed history landing after the modifiers, stack-aware magnitudes, regulation propagation on removal, null-target effects, replace idempotency, group attribution sums, pre-change workers adjusting the committed delta (armor before the clamp).
